{{Top|leg}}
{{Quote|They threatened to make me program the bean juice boiler to detect the presence of impurities, and I'd be tempted (since, doing the programming, I could refrain from defining my own spittle as an "impurity") if not for the fact that they have me working on the pseudonet encryption. It's the most important project around, and I'm just happy they didn't take me off it. |Personal log of Celis Bol|<ref name="CA">{{LivingForce|Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away}}</ref>}}
'''Pseudonet encryption''' was a type of encryption.<ref name="CA" /> Around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="date">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|''Living Force'']] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure ''[[Below the Belt: Philology|Philology]]'' [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten years to the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the events depicted in ''[[Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away|Caaried Away]]'' can therefore be dated to circa [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].</ref> an effort to develop pseudonet encryption was underway at a [[Metatheran Cartel Tilnes base|secret base]] operated by the [[Metatheran Cartel]] trade alliance on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[Tilnes]] and was regarded as the most important project underway at the facility. The [[Caarite]] [[Technician/Legends|technician]] [[Celis Bol]] was assigned to work on the pseudonet encryption project. After Bol was disciplined for [[Water/Legends|spitting]] in the [[bean juice]] of the Cartel base's [[Overseer of Cartel Operations, Tilnes Special Detachment|overseer]] [[Ko Bas]], the technician was permitted to remain on the pseudonet encryption project and not re-assigned as a punishment, much to the Caarite's relief.<ref name="CA" />

{{RPG|Caaried Away}}
18 [[Standard day/Legends|days]] after the incident with the bean juice, a group of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance agents]] ventured to the Cartel base and recovered Bol's log from the installation's [[Computer/Legends|computer]], in which they noted a reference to pseudonet encryption. The agents were unfamiliar with pseudonet encryption and considered it to sound intriguing.<ref name="CA" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
Pseudonet encryption was mentioned in in ''[[Metatheran Caution: Caaried Away|Caaried Away]]'', a [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] released in [[March]] [[2003]] and written by [[Morrie Mullins]]. The adventure formed part of the [[Metatheran Caution trilogy]] of the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|Living Force]] campaign, a supplement to [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]. In the adventure, the player characters roleplay as the freelance agents that travel to the Metatheran Cartel base on Tilnes and it is possible for them to discover a reference to pseudonet encryption within the facility's computer.<ref name="CA" />
